newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh deportees return from Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh deportees return from Saudi Arabia.

text.p: More than 800 Bangladeshis arrived in Chittagong on Thursday after being deported from Saudi Arabia for travelling or staying there illegally for work, port officials said.
The latest arrivals onboard the Hondurus-flagged ship Mecca-1 brought the number of Bangladeshis sent home from Saudi Arabia to nearly 9,000 in two years, they said.
Saudi authorities said some of the deportees had no legal entry or work permits, while others stayed on after their visas expired, Bangladesh officials said.
Returnee Abdul Wahab told Reuters on Thursday that the Saudi government had been continuing a "ruthless expulsion of foreign nationals and so far have pushed out more than 100,000 people".
Wahab had worked as a salesman in Jeddha. His visa expired in February and he was arrested by police while searching for another job.
Wahab said after failing to get his visa extended he had sought help of friends who had been living in Jeddah. "But I was captured by Saudi police and deported," he said.
Most of the deportees arrived without money, and Chittagong port authorities gave them 200 taka ($4.60) each for transport to their homes.
